newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 22.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- The defence forces are making contingency plans to send troops to serve under the NATO-led peace-keeping mission in the former Yugoslavia - possibly within the next few months.
- The Minister for Equality and Law Reform, Murphy Taylor, is to introduce amending legislation to validate up to 50 new marriages retrospectively.
- Allied Irish Bank is making the biggest ever acquisition by an Irish company, paying 1.36 billion dollars for the US bank, Dauphin Deposit Corporation.
-A bitter pre-election dispute had broken out between Labour and the progressive Democrats.
- Ireland's Wednesday budget will be seen as one of the best in modern times, the Prime Minister John Bruton confidently predicted on Tuesday night.
- Wildcat strikes are threatening to disrupt transport on Wednesday as CIE workers vent their anger at a 44 million Irish pound cost-cutting plan.
- Finance Minister, Ruairi Quinn's budget on Wednesday will help put an extra 40,000 people into jobs.
- The continued participation of fringe loyalist parties in the Stormont peace talks was cast into doubt by the British government.
